# Operators

Edva uses Pratt parsing to resolve operator precedence and associativity.
The table below specifies all operator tiers, their Left Binding Power (LBP),
Right Binding Power (RBP), associativity, and semantic groupings.

## Precedence and binding power table

<!-- BEGIN operators.yaml -->
| Tier | LBP | RBP | Operators | Associativity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cycle | 10 | 20 | `@` `@@` `>--` `-->` `--^` | left |
| sequence | 20 | 30 | `;` | left |
| apply | 30 | 30 | `$` | right |
| feed | 40 | 50 | `$>` `$>>` | left |
| choice | 50 | 60 | `|` `[pattern]` `!|` `|->` `|+>` `|-->` `|++>` | left |
| assignment | 60 | 50 | `=` `:=` `+=` `::=` | right |
| range | 70 | 80 | `..` | left |
| logical or | 80 | 90 | `||` | left |
| logical and | 90 | 100 | `&&` | left |
| bitwise or | 100 | 105 | `.|.` | left |
| bitwise xor | 105 | 110 | `.^.` | left |
| bitwise and | 110 | 120 | `.&.` | left |
| comparison | 120 | 130 | `<` `>` `==` `!=` `!<` `!>` | left, same-line |
| shift | 130 | 140 | `.<.` `.>.` | left |
| addition | 140 | 150 | `+` `-` | left |
| multiplication | 150 | 160 | `*` `/` `%` | left |
| unary prefix | 160 | 180 | `!` `+` `&` `++` `.!.` `~~` `?` `??` `-x` `#size` | right |
| postfix / apply | 170 | 180 | `call ()` `.` `::` `: cast` `{N}` `@[...]` `!!` `--!` | left |
| primary | 180 | 180 | `primary` | left |

<!-- END operators.yaml -->

Notable precedence characteristics:

- **Feed vs Apply:** `$>` (left-associative) prepends an argument (`x $> f` $\equiv$ `f(x)`), while `$` (right-associative) appends an argument (`f $ x` $\equiv$ `f(x)`).
- **Choice Absorption:** Both `$` and `$>` sit below the choice tier (tier 5), so an unparenthesized choice expression on the RHS is absorbed as the operand (`a $> b | c | d` $\equiv$ `a $> (b | c | d)`).
- **Binding Powers:** On right-associative tiers such as assignment (LBP 60, RBP 50) and apply (LBP 30, RBP 30), RBP $\le$ LBP allows operators to extend rightward. On left-associative tiers, RBP $>$ LBP forces left binding.

## Values and control flow

- `=` binds an immutable name; a primed identifier is rebindable with `=`.
- `+=` appends to a Builder in place.
- `|` and `[guard]` form choices; `!|` selects a ram's negative branch.
- `|->`, `|+>`, `|-->`, and `|++>` are syntactic shortcuts for early returning unit ramifications (`| --| <->`, `| --| <+>`, `| --| <-->`, `| --| <++>`).
- `@` and `@@` iterate; `-->`, `--^`, and `>--` control cycle escape.
- `--|` performs an early return from an enclosing function (`--| val` with a value, or bare `--|` for void functions).
- `..` forms ranges, including string and slice views.

```{.dva .run}
score = 2
label = score [1] "one" [2] "two" | "other"
```

## Calls and composition

`f(a, b)` calls directly. `$` appends a call argument and is
right-associative; `$>` prepends one and is left-associative. `$>>` chains a
ram with a positive payload (`RamPP` or `RamPN`) through a continuation that must
return a ramification of compatible shape (passing a non-ram continuation emits `E3091`).
When `$` is followed immediately by an indented block, it attaches the block's expressions as a record argument.

```{.dva .run}
#use io

sum: Int, Int => Int
sum = left, right => left + right

io::out $ 2 $> sum(3)
```

## Numeric, logical, and bitwise operators

Arithmetic uses `+ - * / %`; shifts use `.<.` and `.>.`; bitwise operations
use `.|.`, `.^.`, `.&.`, and `.!.`. Bitwise operators accept integerish values only.
Shift sections (`.<. n`, `.>. n`) infer `Int => Int` without explicit type signatures.
Operator sections (`op rhs`) form single-parameter functions over an implicit `_`
with an RHS binding power of 130; `||`, `&&`, `$`, `$>`, `$>>`, `!>`, `!<`, and `!=`
are excluded from forming sections.
Comparisons produce a flag. `&&` and `||` short-circuit; combining heap rams
requires compatible winner layouts, while flags only combine with flags.

`==` and `!=` between two enums perform deep structural equality, comparing
both variant tag and payload value (yielding a bare flag). If a payload type
does not support equality (e.g. function values), comparison is rejected at
compile time (`E3084`). Non-enum ramifications do not support equality (`E3084`).
Relational operators `<` (less), `>` (greater), `!<` (greater-or-equal), and `!>` (less-or-equal)
perform numeric ordering. On floating-point types, `!<` and `!>` follow ordered comparison semantics
(LLVM `OGE` / `OLE`) and evaluate to `<->` (false) if either operand is NaN, distinct from logical
negation `!(x < y)`. Ordering (`<`, `>`, `!<`, `!>`) on any ram or enum is rejected (`E3127`).
Comparing a String with a tuple of strings (`str == (p1, p2, ...)`) tests
concatenated segment equality without allocating. Unary `-` is integer/float negation.

## Type-directed and postfix operators

| Form | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `!flag` | flag negation (flags only; emits E3008 on other types) |
| `+builder` | freeze a Builder into an immutable String (in-place) |
| `&buffer` / `&string` | adjacent unary buffer address for FFI |
| `?value` | byte, element, entry, or field count (`?s`, `?b`, `?a`, `?m`) |
| `??string` | Unicode codepoint count |
| `++value` | copy String, record, slice, or growable array |
| `result!!` | unwrap positive ram payload or abort |
| `result--!` | unwrap or propagate a negative ram from its function |
| `~~lvalue` | two-way state binding lens record `(get = !=> ..., set = v => ...)` |
| `expr {N}` | record repetition |
| `@[addr T]` | volatile typed memory load (`@[addr] = val` for store; `@[addr T] = val` is an error) |
| `#size Type` | compile-time type size |

Arithmetic multiplication (`a * b`) and operator sections (`* 2`) use `*`.
Unary prefix `+` (without trailing space) is Builder freeze; `+ 2` with a space
is the addition section.

Strings and Builders have no member access; use `?` (length), `&` (address),
and `+` (freeze) as appropriate.
